entries.title: Beyond the Penrose Hypothesis: Examining the Association between the Availability of Psychiatric Care and National Homicide Rates
entries.key_finding: Tests Penrose-style bed-availability vs national homicide rates with confounder attention; capacity-violence link at national level.

entries.title: The Penrose Effect and its acceleration by the war on drugs
entries.key_finding: Review: inverse MH-treatment-infrastructure vs incarceration relationship ('Penrose Effect') predictive of deinstitutionalization + mass-incarceration trends, accelerated by criminalization of addiction.

entries.authors: Wild J, Alder L, Weich S et al.
entries.title: The Penrose hypothesis in the second half of the 20th century: investigating the relationship between psychiatric bed numbers and prison populations in England
entries.key_finding: England 1960-2018/19 time-series: prison population vs NHS psychiatric beds (mental illness + ID beds) - tests and largely supportsinverse relation over 60 years.

entries.authors: Allison S, Bastiampillai T, Licinio J et al.
entries.title: When should governments increase the supply of psychiatric beds?
entries.key_finding: Argues low bed supply -> ED boarding, revolving-door readmissions, and is associated with higher suicide risk, premature mortality, homelessness, violent crime and incarceration; transinstitutionalization of SMI.

entries.title: Deinstitutionalisation does not increase imprisonment or homelessness
entries.key_finding: Counterweight: review of 23 deinstitutionalization studies found no homelessness/incarceration/suicide after long-stay discharge - the capacity-crime link is contested, not settled.

entries.authors: Mundt AP, Langerfeldt C, Maphisa J et al. (SSA 2022; EMR 2025; SEAR 2025 series)
entries.title: Changes in rates of psychiatric beds and prison populations in sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2020
entries.key_finding: 46-country retrospective: psychiatric beds (general/forensic/residential) vs prison population rates; same design replicated for Eastern Mediterranean 1990-2022 and Southeast Asia 1990-2024.

entries.authors: Lin CJ, Lin MJ, Jan JF
entries.title: Mental illness, crime and mental health resources: insights from Taiwan using text analysis and spatio-temporal analysis
entries.key_finding: NLP on court judgments to flag mental illness in offenders; spatial-temporal analysis of MH RESOURCES vs crime patterns - closest analog to capacity-vs-prevalence split found.

entries.authors: Park C, Lee JY, Kim JM et al.
entries.title: Comparative Analysis of Violent Crime Statistics in Korea by Mental Illness Status (2012-2022): Implications of Deinstitutionalization
entries.key_finding: National violent-crime series split by offender MH status; evaluates 2017 Korea Mental Health and Welfare Act (harder involuntary commitment) as natural-capacity-shock.
entries.effect_size: annual offender counts with/without mental illness

entries.authors: Khan JR, Hu N, Hodgins M et al.
entries.title: Geospatial clustering of suicide, mental health, sociodemographic and workforce features in Australia
entries.key_finding: Clustering of 294 SA3 regions on suicide rates, MH-condition prevalence, sociodemographics AND mental-health WORKFORCE (capacity) - both constructs co-modeled, suicide endpoint, no crime outcome.
entries.design: Hierarchical clustering on PC components, 294 regions

entries.title: Community mental health under routine detention: jail reliance, pretrial custody, and frequent mental distress
entries.key_finding: County-year CDC PLACES 2018-2023: counties leaning more on jail/pretrial custody have HIGHER prevalence of frequent mental distress - prevalence as DOWNSTREAM of carceral capacity (reverse direction of the pair).

entries.title: Client-Level Effects of States' Mental Health Agency Expenditures and Mental Health Parity Legislation
entries.key_finding: Individual-level data, top-10 vs bottom-10 parity/expenditure states: per-capita MH spending predicts client-level access/outcomes - capacity-input validation.
entries.effect_size: access/outcome differentials top vs bottom decile states

entries.authors: Gu G, Latvala A, Kuja-Halkola R et al.
entries.title: Childhood parental psychiatric hospitalization and offspring suicidal behavior, violent crime, and violent victimization
entries.key_finding: Swedish register: parental psychiatric hospitalization (treatment contact = capacity exposure) vs offspring suicide/violent-crime outcomes. Abstract not populated via EPMC API - record-level only.

entries.authors: Prentice D, Song S, Degli Esposti S et al.
entries.title: Colleges and Crime: Comparing Homicide and Suicide Rates Among College Towns and Their Counterparts
entries.key_finding: County-level homicide AND suicide rates in college towns vs matched counterparts (CDC death certificates 2015-2019): the suicide-homicide co-comparison frame exists institutionally.
entries.effect_size: rates similar overall; higher young-adult firearm homicide risk in college towns

summary: Novelty verdict summary (PAIRING-4): The CAPACITY side is deeply VERIFIED - the Penrose canon (Grecco 2019; Wild 2022 England 1960-2018; Rajkumar 2022 homicide extension; Mundt multi-region bed-vs-prison series; Allison 2018 explicit violent-crime linkage) plus one honest counter-evidence anchor (Salisbury & Thornicroft 2016). The PREVALENCE side is thin and mostly indirect (Li 2026 jail->distress; Taiwan resource-vs-crime 2026; Korea policy shock 2025; Australia workforce+prevalence clustering 2026 with no crime endpoint). NO retrieved study directly pits CAPACITY against PREVALENCE as competing ecological predictors of violent crime/homicide in one design - Khan 2026 co-cluster them for suicide geography only. Suicide-homicide shared structural drivers are partially VERIFIED (deaths-of-despair framing, college-town comparison). => MH-capacity vs MH-prevalence as a rival-predictor question = NOVEL-ANGLE (leaning GAP); capacity-crime association itself = VERIFIED.
